fullPassage: Whenever people on ships use a radio to call for help, they use the word "mayday." But what does it mean? The word was actually selected by a British man named Frederick Mockford in the 1920s. He chose it because it sounds like the French term m'adier, which means "help me." According to standard procedure, the word is to be said three times in a row so that it won't be mistaken for something similar. After this, important information should be given, such as the name and location of the ship. Sometimes, however, one ship will make a mayday call for another ship in trouble. This is called a "mayday relay." It is done when a ship in danger is unable to contact rescuers. A ship hearing the original call may choose to repeatedly perform a mayday relay until help is on the way. This is because when a mayday call is sent, whoever receives it is expected to help out however they can.

det.analysis:

② alike(비슷한) — similar의 유의어예요
③ strange(이상한) — 의미축이 달라 반대가 아니에요

questions.passage: Whenever people on ships use a radio to call for help, they use the word "mayday." But what does it mean? The word was actually selected by a British man named Frederick Mockford in the 1920s. He chose it because it sounds like the French term m'adier, which means "help me." According to standard procedure, the word is to be said three times in a row so that it won't be mistaken for something similar. After this, important information should be given, such as the name and location of the ship. Sometimes, however, one ship will make a mayday call for another ship in trouble. This is called a "mayday relay." It is done when a ship in danger is unable to contact rescuers. A ship hearing the <u>original</u> call may choose to repeatedly perform a mayday relay until help is on the way. This is because when a mayday call is sent, whoever receives it is expected to help out however they can.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 original과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: original=최초의 / first=첫 번째의 / initial=처음의 / subsequent=그 이후의 / genuine=진짜의
det.analysis:

② initial(처음의) — original의 유의어예요
③ subsequent(그 이후의) — '최초의(original)'와 반대로 '뒤이어 오는'이라는 뜻이라 반의어예요 ←정답
④ genuine(진짜의) — original의 '진짜의'라는 다른 뜻과 오히려 통해요(함정)
det.tip: 여기서 original = 최초의(the original call). 반대 = subsequent(그 이후의). genuine은 다른 뜻(진짜의)이라 함정

det.analysis: name을 과거분사 named로 바꿔요. 'a British man named Frederick Mockford(프레더릭 모크퍼드라는 이름의 영국인)'처럼, 명사(man) 뒤에 과거분사 named가 와서 '~라는 이름의'라는 뜻으로 앞의 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 사람이 이름을 '지어 받은' 것이므로 수동의 뜻인 과거분사를 써요.
det.tip: 명사 + named + 이름 = ~라는 이름의 (과거분사 후치수식)
